title: Ethical Use: A Pre-Pre-Suasive Consideration
coreMove: Decide whether the attention plan should be used before deciding how to use it.
sourcePressure: The source says the first decision is ethical use, warns that profit can outrank ethics, and argues unethical tactics undermine organizational profits in three ways without naming them in the sidecar.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Ethics is a compliance note after the persuasive design is finished.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: a growth lead deciding whether to hide cancellation terms
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether profit pressure is checked before the attention tactic is built
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead circles the hidden-fee revenue line, then writes the likely trust cost beside it before approving copy
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pricing mockup beside a revenue forecast

exampleSpecs.audience: a marketing manager weighing fear-based refill messages
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a health cue informs or exploits patient anxiety
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager reads the message aloud beside the patient opt-out list before sending it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a campaign screen with the opt-out count visible

exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cue targets the parent’s decision or bypasses the child’s restraint
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the designer removes the countdown sparkle after watching a child press buy before reading the price
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tablet screen frozen on a sparkling countdown

exampleSpecs.audience: a fundraising director choosing images for relief donations
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether attention honors the people pictured or turns suffering into a lever
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director rejects the most shocking image after checking consent notes and need specificity
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a contact sheet beside a consent log

exampleSpecs.audience: an HR manager deciding whether to prefill employee goals
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the design supports agency or manufactures agreement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager watches a tester erase a prefilled goal and marks the coercion risk before launch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wellness form with a prefilled goal highlighted

exampleSpecs.audience: a finance director auditing add-on warranty prompts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the pre-suasive frame creates informed choice or confusion
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director has a clerk explain the warranty with the total payment visible and stops the script when the cost is hidden
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a payment worksheet with add-on rows exposed

skillTargets: run the ethical decision before tactic design
identify when profit pressure corrupts pre-suasion
forecast trust costs from manipulative frames

tryThisNowSpec: Before polishing a persuasive cue, write who benefits, who could be misled, and what trust cost would make the tactic unacceptable.
